title: Fix: policy propagation race causing stale rollout weights in one region (monotonic versions + retries)
author: Jordan Lee
description: Context: We hit an issue where edited Hosted rollout weights would correctly apply in most regions, but one region (observed in eu-west-1) could continue serving the previous weights for minutes. This showed up as "unexpected traffic split after editing rollout weights" (SUP-4027) and was reproducible under concurrent rapid edits (Console wizard stepper) + transient propagation lag. Root cause: the rollout policy propagation path had an out-of-order write/observe race between (1) the control-plane publisher sending policy updates and (2) the regional config applier persisting the resolved routing weights. Under certain timing, an older policy revision could be applied after a newer revision, effectively rolling the region back to stale weights without any further correction until the next edit. Fix: Make regional application monotonic by policy version and add bounded retries on detectably stale updates. We now (a) carry the policy revision/version through the propagation envelope, (b) persist the last-applied revision per (account_id, route_id, region) and refuse to apply any update with revision <= last_applied_revision, and (c) if we detect an out-of-order update we re-fetch latest from the control plane (read-through) and retry apply with exponential backoff (jittered) up to a small bound. Also adds metrics/logging so we can see when we drop stale updates and how often we need to retry. Scope: control plane propagation worker + regional applier + tests. Notes: This does not change the external policy schema; it is an internal propagation correctness fix. It should reduce the chance of "split drift" and prevent silent regression to prior weights. Testing: added unit tests for monotonic apply and an integration test that simulates rapid edits with reordered delivery; validated in staging by repeatedly editing weights 10%->30%->5% while injecting artificial delay on eu-west-1 subscriber.
commits: control-plane: include policy_revision in rollout propagation envelope
regional-applier: track last_applied_revision and enforce monotonic apply
regional-applier: retry loop w/ read-through fetch on stale/out-of-order updates
obs: add counters for stale_update_dropped and apply_retry_count + structured logs
tests: out-of-order delivery simulation + regression coverage for rapid edits
conversation:
Ethan Park (reviewer): Can you clarify why we need both the monotonic guard and the retry? If we drop stale updates, wouldn't the next update fix it anyway?

Jordan Lee (author): In the failure mode we saw, the "stale" update was the last event delivered to that region (newer event already delivered + applied, then older arrives late and overwrites). If we only drop, we'd be fine; but we also saw cases where the region missed the newer event entirely due to transient subscriber errors. The retry is specifically for "stale/out-of-order" detection to force a read-through fetch of the latest policy so the region converges without waiting for another user edit.

Mina Haddad (reviewer): For routing correctness: is revision tracked per route or per policy object? We need to ensure a per-route rollout update doesn't block unrelated routing config updates.

Jordan Lee (author): Per (account_id, route_id, region) and keyed to rollout_policy_revision (the resolved routing object for that route). Non-rollout routing updates use a different path; within this path we only compare against the same route's last_applied_revision.

Sean Gallagher (reviewer): Please add an upper bound to retries + ensure we don't hammer control plane on sustained churn. Also want a metric + log when we drop as stale so oncall can see it.

Jordan Lee (author): Done. Retries capped at 4 attempts with jittered backoff (50ms base, max ~800ms) and we only do read-through on stale detection (not on generic errors). Added metrics: rollouts.propagation.stale_update_dropped and rollouts.propagation.apply_retry_count with region tag (bounded set). Logs include account_id/route_id, incoming_rev, last_applied_rev, region, and action=drop|retry.

Allison Grant (reviewer): Cardinality: route_id in logs is fine, but please ensure metrics do NOT include route_id. Also can we add a dashboard panel / alert later?

Jordan Lee (author): Metrics are region-only + result code; no route_id. Agree on dashboard follow-up; I left a TODO in ENG-8425 and noted in the SRE channel.

Benji Okafor (reviewer): Migration: where do we initialize last_applied_revision for existing rows? If default is 0, does that cause any issue for in-flight updates during deploy?

Jordan Lee (author): last_applied_revision defaults to 0; first apply after deploy will accept any rev > 0 (all our rollout_policy v2 revisions start at 1). During deploy, a region on old binary may still apply without monotonic checks; but once upgraded it will refuse regressions. The publisher already includes revision; this is backwards compatible (older subscribers ignore the field).

Mina Haddad (reviewer): Nit: can we rename "policy_version" to "policy_revision" consistently? Avoid confusion with schema version.

Jordan Lee (author): Updated names across envelope + store fields to revision.

Ethan Park (reviewer): Approve after rename + add a regression test that reproduces the late-arriving-old-update overwrite.

Jordan Lee (author): Added test: deliver rev=10, apply; then deliver rev=9, assert drop; also a variant where rev=10 delivery is dropped and rev=9 triggers read-through to fetch rev=10 and apply.

Sean Gallagher (reviewer): Approved. Please coordinate release with Connor (releases) since this is hotfix-worthy for GA beta customers.

Jordan Lee (author): Sync’d with Connor; landing to main and will cherry-pick to release branch if needed for staged rollout.

Merge: Squashed and merged by Ethan Park on 2024-10-04. Post-merge note: Staging validation run completed; production rollout scheduled for next regional deploy window with extra monitoring on split-drift dashboards.
